key_insight: Machine learning can improve computer algebra by guiding costly symbolic algorithms or performing symbolic computations directly.
engineering_relevance: ML-guided algorithm selection and heuristics could reduce computational costs in symbolic workflows used for scientific and engineering analysis.
method: Systematically review ML applications in computer algebra.
Compare approaches ranging from decision trees to transformers.
Cover cylindrical algebraic decomposition, Gröbner bases, symbolic integration, and other tasks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a literature synthesis rather than new performance results and identifies missing benchmark datasets as a barrier to reliable comparison.
watch_item: Limited benchmarks hinder assessment of model generalizability; symbolic outputs also require mathematical verification.
paper_title: A Survey on the Use of Machine Learning within Computer Algebra
